name: Control: piecewise-constant mean
equations: jump_t ~ Bern(hazard); mu_t = clip(mu_{t-1} + jump_t N(0, magnitude), 30, 170); d_t = max(0, mu_t + sigma N(0,1)); y_t = d_t + tau N(0,1)
breaks: Nothing: this is the process the correctly specified model assumes.

name: A. Long stability, unannounced reversal
equations: mu_t = mu_0 for t < c; mu_0 - direction * magnitude for t >= c; c ~ U{0.35T, 0.60T}; further reversals at rate hazard
information: y_0..y_{t-1}; the change time c is researcher-only
breaks: Constant hazard: the change time is not geometric, and a long quiet spell is not evidence of stability.

name: B. Heavy tails and rare contamination
equations: d_t = max(0, mu_t + sigma e_t); e_t ~ N(0,1) w.p. 1-0.05, (magnitude/sigma) T_3 w.p. 0.05 [variant student_t: e_t ~ standardized T_3 every period]
breaks: Gaussian outcomes: the likelihood every filter uses, and the sample mean the window models use, are both non-robust.

name: C. Outcomes outside the observed support
equations: d_t truncated to mu_0 +- 2 sigma for t < 0.45T; thereafter an excursion of size magnitude beyond the historical extreme with probability hazard
breaks: Empirical support: a model that can only reweight observed values cannot price an outcome it has never seen.

name: D. Multimodal demand, moving mode probabilities
equations: modes at mu_0 -+ magnitude/2 (three_mode adds mu_0); logit(w_t) walks by N(0, 1.2) when Bern(hazard); k_t ~ Cat(w_t); d_t = max(0, m_{k_t} + sigma N(0,1))
information: y_0..y_{t-1}; the active mode k_t is researcher-only
breaks: Unimodality: the predictive mean sits between the modes, at a demand that almost never occurs.

name: E. Decision-dependent uncertainty
equations: level: g_t = 0.9 g_{t-1} + 0.35 lost_{t-1}; mu_t = clip(b_t - g_t, 30, 170); regime: hazard_t = hazard (1 + 6 * 1{stocked out at t-1})
information: y_0..y_{t-1}; mu_t and the realized hazard are researcher-only
breaks: Exogeneity: every model here treats the demand process as unaffected by its own orders.
